newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sees 97 wheat output at three mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sees 97 wheat output at three mln tonnes.

text.p: Bulgaria expects to produce enough wheat this year to satisfy domestic needs until the next crop and meet export commitments, an official said on Tuesday.
Valeri Iliev, head of the plant-growing department at the agriculture ministry, told Reuters he saw 1997 wheat production at some 3.0 million tonnes, up from last year's 1.8 million.

"The expected wheat output of three million tonnes will enable the country to meet its consumption of some 1.6 million tonnes and to return the wheat which has been bought in exchange for future exports from this crop," Iliev said.
Bulgaria received 100,000 tonnes of wheat from Poland in March to ease an acute grain shortage against an agreement to export the same quantity of wheat from the new crop.
The country also awarded contracts to Swiss firm Glencore and Bulgaria's Nada to import 100,000 tonnes of wheat against forward contracts to export 134,000 tonnes from the new crop.
Another 35,000 tonnes of the new crop were approved for a barter deal involving combine harvesters and other equipment badly needed by Bulgaria.
"As cultivation of the autumn crops is proceeding well, I think the expected output is realistic," said Iliev.
Bulgaria planted 1.5 million hectares to wheat and barley, up from 1.27 million hectares previously.
Excessive wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest last year created acute grain shortages early this year, which have been overcome in the past three months.
